highlights: Cubelets is a magnetic construction platform with Sense, Action and Think blocks; behavior emerges from the arrangement and optional Console/mobile tools add Blockly, C and remote control. Discovery and educator sets are packages; module names and module years do not define additional whole-robot models or a family launch date.

Selected public documentation distinguishes the generic GoPiGo kit from historical GoPiGo 2 and GoPiGo 3 hardware. GoPiGo 2 has 65 mm wheels and optical encoders; GoPiGo 3 has 66.5 mm wheels and magnetic encoders. Whole-robot dimensions, runtime and linear speed are not inferred from these figures.

The current generic GoPiGo 199 USD package includes rechargeable battery/charger, sensor and servo hardware but excludes Raspberry Pi. The historical 99 USD GoPiGo 3 Base Kit excludes Pi, microSD and eight AA batteries. An update notice names GoPiGo Core; its distinct hardware identity remains unresolved rather than counted twice.

Pi 5 support differs by software scope: the generic GoPiGo kit page excludes it, while the GoPiGo 3 Raspberry Pi OS README supports it with power-consumption and button cautions. GoBox, PyBox and project packs are teaching subscriptions/materials; BrickPi is a controller platform requiring separate review.

GiggleBot’s official MakeCode library documents two line and two light sensors, wheeled motor control and optional servo/distance-sensor expansion. A laser-based distance sensor is not established as included. The old 60 USD kit snapshot excludes micro: bit; failed fresh TLS/connection checks are not refreshed offer evidence.

This batch reviews five selected family/generation identities, not the complete historical portfolio. Optional parts, arbitrary construction configurations and bundle names are not inflated into whole robots. Current stock, standardized independent performance, exclusive USPs and market/search leadership remain unproven.
